import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Set style
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-darkgrid')
sns.set_palette("husl")

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create figure with subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(18, 12))

# 1. Price distribution by sensor type
ax1 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 1)
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='sensor_type', y='price_usd', order=df.groupby('sensor_type')['price_usd'].median().sort_values().index)
ax1.set_title('Camera Price Distribution by Sensor Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Sensor Type')
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)')
ax1.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 2. Megapixels vs Price with sensor type coloring
ax2 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 2)
scatter = ax2.scatter(df['megapixels'], df['price_usd'], c=df['max_iso'], 
                      cmap='viridis', alpha=0.6, s=50, edgecolors='w', linewidth=0.5)
ax2.set_title('Megapixels vs Price (colored by Max ISO)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xlabel('Megapixels')
ax2.set_ylabel('Price (USD)')
cbar = plt.colorbar(scatter, ax=ax2)
cbar.set_label('Max ISO')

# 3. Camera count by brand (top 10)
ax3 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 3)
top_brands = df['brand'].value_counts().head(10)
bars = ax3.barh(top_brands.index, top_brands.values)
ax3.set_title('Top 10 Camera Brands by Count', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_xlabel('Number of Cameras')
ax3.invert_yaxis()
for i, v in enumerate(top_brands.values):
    ax3.text(v + 0.5, i, str(v), va='center')

# 4. Weight vs Price by body type
ax4 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 4)
for body_type in df['body_type'].unique():
    subset = df[df['body_type'] == body_type]
    ax4.scatter(subset['weight_grams'], subset['price_usd'], label=body_type, alpha=0.7, s=60)
ax4.set_title('Weight vs Price by Body Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_xlabel('Weight (grams)')
ax4.set_ylabel('Price (USD)')
ax4.legend(title='Body Type', fontsize=9)

# 5. Price trend over model years
ax5 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 5)
year_stats = df.groupby('model_year')['price_usd'].agg(['mean', 'median', 'std']).reset_index()
ax5.plot(year_stats['model_year'], year_stats['mean'], 'o-', linewidth=2, markersize=6, label='Mean Price')
ax5.fill_between(year_stats['model_year'], 
                 year_stats['mean'] - year_stats['std'], 
                 year_stats['mean'] + year_stats['std'], 
                 alpha=0.2, label='±1 Std Dev')
ax5.set_title('Camera Price Trend Over Model Years', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax5.set_xlabel('Model Year')
ax5.set_ylabel('Price (USD)')
ax5.legend()
ax5.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 6. 4K Video capability by sensor type
ax6 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 6)
video_data = df.groupby(['sensor_type', 'has_video_4k']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
video_data_percentage = video_data.div(video_data.sum(axis=1), axis=0) * 100
video_data_percentage.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True, ax=ax6, color=['#FF6B6B', '#4ECDC4'])
ax6.set_title('4K Video Capability by Sensor Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax6.set_xlabel('Sensor Type')
ax6.set_ylabel('Percentage (%)')
ax6.legend(['No 4K', 'Has 4K'], title='4K Video')
ax6.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# Adjust layout and save
plt.suptitle('Digital Camera Market Analysis: Specifications and Pricing Trends', 
             fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150, facecolor='white')
plt.close()
